sections.content: How many people stayed in Carlton in Lindrick after gaining qualifications?

Carlton in Lindrick is a small town in the East Midlands. Carlton in Lindrick does not have its own university.

Carlton in Lindrick has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Carlton in Lindrick ended up with:

  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 260 state-school pupils from Carlton in Lindrick who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 60 (23%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 65 (25%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Carlton in Lindrick to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Carlton in Lindrick's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Carlton in Lindrick in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

In 2018 to 2019, 50% of qualified non-graduates living in Carlton in Lindrick had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 80 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Carlton in Lindrick, compared with the 65 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 50% of qualified (level 3+) non-graduates in Carlton in Lindrick had also lived there when they sat their GCSEs, while 50% had moved there from elsewhere.
